title: Google Hotels Prices — input

queries.title: Places
queries.description: Place searches as typed into Google Hotels, e.g. ["hotels in Lisbon"], ["hotels near Times Square"], ["5-star hotels Bangkok Sukhumvit"]. Returns up to maxHotels hotels per place. Write the place exactly and add the country when it is ambiguous ("hotels in Barcelona Spain"): Google never fails a place search, a misspelt place is matched to somewhere else and those hotels are billed. After the run check the status row: spread_km (large = wrong or vague place) and each hotel's lat/lng.

hotelNames.title: Hotels by name
hotelNames.description: Exact hotels by name, no URL needed, e.g. ["Hyatt Regency Lisbon", "Altis Grand Hotel Lisbon"] (add the city; "Hotel Artemide, Rome" with a comma works too). Use for "what does each booking site charge for hotel X" and for rate parity. A Google Maps place link works too, and names in Chinese, Japanese, Korean or Thai. A name that matches nothing costs nothing and is reported in a status row; only a hotel whose name matches yours is billed. Filters and maxHotels do not apply to named hotels.

checkIn.title: Check-in
checkIn.description: Check-in date: "2026-10-03" (YYYY-MM-DD), or relative to the day the run starts: "30 days", "6 weeks", "tomorrow". Use relative dates for scheduled runs ("track prices daily"): the input never needs editing. A past date is rejected before anything is charged.

checkOut.title: Check-out
checkOut.description: Check-out date, after checkIn: "2026-10-06", or relative: "32 days". Nights = checkOut minus checkIn, so checkIn "30 days" + checkOut "32 days" = a 2-night stay starting 30 days after each run.

adults.title: Adults
adults.description: Adults in the room, 1 to 6, e.g. 2 (default 2). Google prices ONE room for the whole party: there is no rooms input, and above 6 adults Google returns no price at all.

childrenAges.title: Children (ages)
childrenAges.description: Ages of the children in the same room, e.g. [5, 9] for two children aged 5 and 9. Empty (default) = no children. The price is for one room holding the adults plus these children.

currency.title: Currency
currency.description: ISO 4217 code for every price in the run, e.g. "EUR". Any currency Google supports: USD, EUR, GBP, JPY, THB, SGD, AUD, AED, … Left empty the actor uses "USD". When the user names no currency, pass the destination's ("EUR" for Paris).

maxHotels.title: Max hotels per place
maxHotels.description: Hotels to return per place search and stay, 1 to 200, e.g. 50 (default 20). Filters and sortBy are applied by Google BEFORE this cap: 30 with sortBy "lowest_price" = the 30 cheapest matching hotels, and fewer come back only when fewer match. The main cost control: at most maxHotels × $0.004 per place and stay, plus offer rows while includeOffers is true. The largest cities end near 185 hotels.

sortBy.title: Sort by
sortBy.description: Google Hotels' own order for place searches: "relevance" (default), "lowest_price", "highest_rating", "most_reviewed". Use with maxHotels for "the 30 cheapest" or "the 40 best-rated hotels". Applied to every stay of a sweep separately. "lowest_price" is Google Hotels' own cheapest-first order for the stay.

includeOffers.title: Fetch every source's rates
includeOffers.description: true (DEFAULT) adds separate type="offer" rows at $0.002 each, plus $0.004/hotel. Offers: source, official, nightly, total, currency, link, partner_url; join by entity_id + check_in + check_out. Set false for one lowest price per hotel without OTA rates. For comparison keep true. maxOffersPerHotel=N>0 caps each hotel/stay at $0.004+N×$0.002; 0 is uncapped. official:true marks the hotel site only when Google lists it; a cap can omit it. Links may be null.

offerLevel.title: Offer rows per hotel
offerLevel.description: "sources" (default) keeps each booking site's lowest rate. "rooms" adds room/rate variants, names, max guests and cancellation deadlines. Observed room-level sample: average 65, high 150 offers/hotel; not a cap. Both modes obey maxOffersPerHotel: N>0 keeps only the N cheapest offers and can omit the official site. Per hotel/stay ≤$0.004+N×$0.002. For a run ceiling use call-actor callOptions.maxTotalChargeUsd, outside input. Ignored when includeOffers=false.

includeDetails.title: Hotel details
includeDetails.description: true = each hotel row also gets address, phone, Google Maps place_id, long description, amenities by name (about 120, e.g. "Wi-Fi (free)", "Indoor pool", "Parking (extra charge)"), amenities_unavailable, rating_breakdown (5 to 1 stars), review_aspects (Service, Location, Breakfast… with positive and negative counts), external_ratings (Tripadvisor…) and photos. No extra charge. Default false. Also fills star class, rating and coordinates for hotels given by URL.

sweepDays.title: Sweep check-in over N more days
sweepDays.description: 0 (default) = only the stay above. N = repeat the same length of stay for each of the next N check-in days, e.g. checkIn "2026-11-02", checkOut "2026-11-04", sweepDays 13 = 14 two-night stays with check-ins 2 to 15 Nov. Use for a price calendar or "which day is cheapest". Every stay is billed as its own rows, so cost × (N + 1): set includeOffers false to keep it low. Maximum 60.

freeCancellation.title: Free cancellation only
freeCancellation.description: true = only hotels with a free-cancellation rate for the dates. Google then quotes that refundable rate as the hotel's nightly price, and maxPrice applies to it. Default false. Place searches only.

maxPrice.title: Maximum price per night
maxPrice.description: Highest nightly price in `currency`, e.g. 250. 0 (default) = no maximum. Google applies it to the nightly price it displays (the `nightly` field), before maxHotels, so hotels above it are never returned or billed. Place searches only.

minRating.title: Guest rating
minRating.description: Minimum Google guest rating out of 5, as a string: "3.5", "4.0" or "4.5" (Google offers only these steps). Default "any".

hotelClass.title: Hotel class (stars)
hotelClass.description: Star classes to keep, as strings: ["4", "5"] = 4-star and 5-star hotels only. Allowed: "2", "3", "4", "5". Empty (default) = any class.

amenities.title: Amenities
amenities.description: Only hotels that have ALL of these, e.g. ["pool", "free_breakfast"]. Google Hotels' own filters: free_wifi, free_breakfast, restaurant, bar, kid_friendly, pet_friendly, free_parking, parking, ev_charger, room_service, fitness_center, spa, pool (any pool), indoor_pool, outdoor_pool, air_conditioned, wheelchair_accessible, beach_access, all_inclusive. Empty (default) = no filter. To LIST each hotel's amenities use includeDetails.

country.title: Market
country.description: Google market (gl): any 2-letter country code, e.g. "gb", "pt", "jp". Default "us". It is the country of the person searching, NOT the destination: keep "us" unless the user wants prices as seen from a country. It changes which booking sites are listed (Klook, Traveloka, Wego in Asian markets).

language.title: Language
language.description: Google language (hl), e.g. "en", "ja", "zh-CN", "es", "de". Default "en". Sets the language of hotel names (where Google has a translation), room names, class labels and deal notes. Queries and hotelNames may be written in any language.

hotels.title: Specific hotels
hotels.description: Exact hotels by Google Hotels URL (https://www.google.com/travel/hotels/entity/ChkI…) or entity token, e.g. the `entity_id` or `google_url` of rows from an earlier run. Use to price the SAME set of hotels every day: run a place search once, then pass its entity_id values here. Filters and maxHotels do not apply. Add includeDetails for star class, rating and coordinates.
hotels.sectionCaption: More ways to pick hotels and cap cost

maxOffersPerHotel.title: Max offer rows per hotel
maxOffersPerHotel.description: 0 (default) = all available offer rows, not a cost cap. N>0 keeps the N cheapest offers per hotel/stay: at most $0.004+N×$0.002 including its hotel row. Example: 10 hotels with N=8 cost at most $0.20. A cap can omit the official-site offer; report a missing direct price rather than concluding parity. Use call-actor callOptions.maxTotalChargeUsd outside input for a run ceiling.

minPrice.title: Minimum price per night
minPrice.description: Lowest nightly price in `currency`, e.g. 80. 0 (default) = no minimum. Applied by Google before maxHotels. Place searches only.

specialOffers.title: Special offers only
specialOffers.description: true = only hotels Google marks as a deal for the dates; `deal` carries the note ("23% less than usual") and `deal_percent` the number. Default false. Place searches only.

proxyConfiguration.title: Proxy
proxyConfiguration.description: Google accepts Apify datacenter proxies for these calls; keep the default. Residential is unnecessary.

sessions.title: Parallel proxy sessions
sessions.description: Concurrent egress IPs; each is paced at perIp requests per second.

perIp.title: Requests per second per IP
perIp.description: Pace per proxy session. 0.5 is safe; raise carefully.

description: Google Hotels prices. Minimal input: {"queries":["hotels in Lisbon"],"checkIn":"30 days","checkOut":"33 days"}. Output is flat: type=hotel/offer/status. Join hotel and offer rows by entity_id + check_in + check_out; hotel_id may be null. Offers contain source, official, nightly, total, currency, link and partner_url. includeOffers=true (default) adds $0.002/offer to $0.004/hotel; set false for one lowest-rate hotel row. Optional fields can be null.
